approvalRequirements: Be an eligible National Grid commercial natural-gas customer at a qualifying Upstate New York service location.
Select a currently eligible prescriptive gas measure, building-envelope measure, or project accepted through the applicable custom or whole-building pathway.
Submit the required project or rebate information and obtain written preapproval before purchase or installation when the selected pathway requires it.
Install equipment that meets the published technical specifications and code requirements.
Submit invoices, equipment documentation, and any requested savings records, and allow inspection or other verification before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: National Grid uses published prescriptive and project-specific incentive pathways rather than competitive scoring. A qualifying, documented project is likely to be paid after review and verification while funds remain, although several mapped measures fall outside the current gas-program scope.
reviews.evidenceText: Current National Grid materials provide prescriptive incentives for qualifying commercial gas equipment and project-based support for eligible efficiency work, with applications, technical review, documentation, and verification before payment.

approvalRequirements: Be a National Grid Massachusetts residential electric customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install eligible residential EV charging wiring or a qualifying charger during the current program year.
Use a licensed electrician for eligible 208- or 240-volt wiring work and satisfy the program's circuit and equipment requirements.
Submit the current application with itemized invoices, proof of installation, photographs, and required EV or charger information by the published deadline.
Enroll qualifying smart-charger projects in the applicable off-peak or discount-rate program and allow National Grid to verify the installation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current program has objective customer, wiring, charger, documentation, and enrollment conditions. A complete qualifying claim is likely to receive the published rebate after routine review, subject to available funds.
reviews.evidenceText: National Grid's current Massachusetts materials require an eligible residential account, qualifying EV charging work, invoices and installation proof, and measure-specific off-peak enrollment or verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Nebraska Public Power District retail customer or customer of a participating wholesale utility.
Purchase and permanently install new equipment that meets the current EnergyWise commercial measure specifications.
Obtain utility approval before purchase or installation when the incentive amount or project type triggers preapproval, including larger or custom projects.
Submit the signed current-year application with proof of purchase, installation details, and required technical documentation.
Allow the utility to inspect the site or equipment before or after installation and comply with program limits and available funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: EnergyWise incentives are generally rules-based and paid after eligibility and documentation review. A qualifying prescriptive project is likely to be awarded, with advance approval and additional review for larger or custom projects.
reviews.evidenceText: The current EnergyWise program publishes commercial incentives and applications requiring eligible new equipment, proof of purchase, utility review, and inspection, with advance approval for specified larger projects.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible NPPD retail customer or customer of a participating wholesale utility.
For a residential claim, purchase and install qualifying Level 2 charging equipment and submit proof of purchase and installation.
For a commercial project, submit the applicable application, site and equipment information, cost documentation, and required bids.
Obtain written preapproval before ordering or installing a DC fast charger and satisfy public-access and other measure-specific requirements.
Complete installation, submit the final payment request and supporting records, and allow utility verification before reimbursement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current GoEV offerings use published residential and commercial eligibility rules. A compliant Level 2 claim or preapproved commercial project is likely to receive the stated incentive after documentation and verification, subject to funding.
reviews.evidenceText: NPPD's current GoEV program provides residential and commercial charging incentives, requires applications and supporting cost records, and requires advance approval for DC fast-charging projects.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible residential customer of NPPD or a participating wholesale utility.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying residential measure that meets the applicable efficiency and installation specifications.
Use the current measure-specific application and provide proof of purchase, model and efficiency information, and required contractor or installation documentation.
Complete any required assessment, testing, or verification for insulation, heat-pump, water-heating, or other performance-based measures.
Submit within the current program period and comply with customer, quantity, incentive, and available-funding limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The residential incentives are prescriptive and use objective measure and documentation requirements. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be paid after utility compliance review, subject to current limits and funds.
reviews.evidenceText: Current EnergyWise residential materials list qualifying measures and require current applications, purchase and installation evidence, technical eligibility, and utility review or verification.

approvalRequirements: Wait for and respond to a Nevada NEVI solicitation or procurement that is open to the applicant's project type.
Propose charging infrastructure at an eligible site and satisfy the applicable federal and state equipment, uptime, public-access, corridor, utility, permitting, and readiness requirements.
Submit a complete proposal by the solicitation deadline with required technical, financial, ownership, environmental, and implementation documentation.
Provide any required nonfederal match and pass administrative screening and competitive evaluation.
Receive formal selection and execute the state agreement before beginning reimbursable work.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Nevada's approved NEVI plan establishes authority to proceed, but the current official materials reviewed do not identify an open applicant solicitation with project-specific selection criteria, funding, and deadlines. Award probability cannot be determined without that procurement evidence.
reviews.evidenceText: Nevada DOT states that its updated NEVI plan has federal approval and describes competitive grant procedures generally, but a current Nevada NEVI applicant notice and award process were not verified.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Braunfels Utilities customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install qualifying central air-conditioning, heat-pump, or smart-thermostat equipment that meets the current efficiency and installation requirements.
Submit the applicable current rebate application with account, equipment, contractor, and installation information.
Provide itemized invoices, model and efficiency documentation, photographs or other supporting records requested by NBU.
Allow NBU to verify the installation and comply with current incentive caps and available funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: NBU publishes fixed or capped rebates with objective equipment and documentation rules. A timely, complete qualifying HVAC or thermostat claim is likely to be paid after review and verification while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Current NBU materials list HVAC, heat-pump, and smart-thermostat rebates and require customer and equipment eligibility, completed applications, invoices, and installation documentation.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Oregon business customer of Portland General Electric or Pacific Power for the current battery-storage offering.
Install a battery system meeting the current minimum capacity and other Solar program technical requirements.
Use the current Solar program application process and obtain an incentive reservation before installation when required.
Use an eligible contractor or trade ally and complete installation within the reservation and program deadlines.
Submit final invoices, permits, jurisdictional approval, commissioning or interconnection records, and other required completion documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Energy Trust currently lists an active business battery-storage incentive with a defined reservation and completion pathway. However, that offering is administered through the Solar program rather than the named New Buildings opportunity, so the source-to-opportunity routing must be corrected before treating the award as routine.
reviews.evidenceText: Energy Trust's current Solar materials show an active business battery-storage incentive requiring program application, funds reservation, qualifying equipment, installation, and final approval. The incentive is not documented as part of the named New Buildings program.

approvalRequirements: Be a Silicon Valley Power nonresidential customer undertaking an eligible new building, addition, or major renovation in Santa Clara.
Submit the current application and project plans before purchasing or installing incentivized equipment.
Demonstrate that the proposed lighting, HVAC, water-heating, or other eligible systems exceed the applicable code or program baseline.
Receive written preapproval identifying the approved incentive amount and project-completion deadline.
Complete the approved work, submit invoices and required technical records, and pass post-installation inspection before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current application establishes a rules-based preapproval and inspection process with published incentive calculations. A project that receives written approval and is completed as approved is likely to be paid, subject to program funds and caps.
reviews.evidenceText: Silicon Valley Power requires new-construction applicants to apply before installation, obtain written preapproval, meet code-improvement and equipment criteria, complete the project on time, and pass final documentation and inspection review.

approvalRequirements: Submit a complete proposal under New Hampshire DOT RFP NH-DOT-2027-01 by the published August 21, 2026 deadline.
Propose eligible DC fast-charging infrastructure at a location and configuration permitted by the RFP.
Satisfy NEVI and other federal requirements for equipment, public access, reliability, cybersecurity, Buy America, operations, maintenance, reporting, and data sharing.
Provide the required site control, utility coordination, permits, project-readiness evidence, budget, schedule, and nonfederal match.
Pass administrative and competitive evaluation and execute a state contract before beginning reimbursable work.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: New Hampshire has an active competitive RFP, but proposals are evaluated and only selected projects receive contracts within available funding. Compliance is necessary but does not make an award automatic.
reviews.evidenceText: New Hampshire DOT announced a current Round II NEVI request for proposals with an August 21, 2026 deadline. Awards require a responsive proposal, federal compliance, competitive evaluation, and contract execution.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Hampshire Electric Co-op commercial or municipal member.
Contact or apply to the program before committing to work when the selected custom, new-construction, EV, or other project pathway requires advance review.
Install currently qualifying equipment or implement an accepted custom measure that satisfies the technical and savings requirements.
Submit project descriptions, calculations where applicable, equipment specifications, invoices, and other required documentation.
Complete any required inspection, commissioning, or savings verification before incentive payment while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: NHEC and NHSaves offer prescriptive and custom commercial incentives under published technical pathways. A qualifying prescriptive claim or preapproved custom project is likely to be paid after completion review and verification, subject to funding.
reviews.evidenceText: Current NHEC and NHSaves materials provide commercial and municipal efficiency incentives for qualifying equipment and custom projects, with early program coordination, supporting documentation, and verification requirements.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible NHEC residential member financing a project accepted under the current energy-efficiency loan offering.
Obtain and submit an acceptable project proposal or contractor estimate before applying for financing.
For on-bill financing, satisfy the cooperative's account and excellent-payment-history requirements and remain within the published loan amount and term.
For third-party financing, complete the lender application and satisfy its independent credit and underwriting criteria.
Execute the financing documents and provide invoices or completion documentation required for funding or the interest-rate subsidy.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program provides defined financing routes, but approval depends on account history or independent lender underwriting in addition to project eligibility. A qualifying retrofit alone does not assure financing.
reviews.evidenceText: NHEC currently offers limited on-bill financing based on payment history and a larger third-party loan with an interest subsidy, contractor-proposal requirements, and lender credit approval.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible NHEC residential member at the installation address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying heat pump, heat-pump water heater, appliance, weatherization measure, or other listed product.
Meet the applicable equipment ratings, sizing, contractor, installation, and existing-system requirements.
Submit the current online or measure-specific application with invoices, model information, installation records, and required photographs or certifications.
Complete any required whole-home, electric-resistance-displacement, or post-installation verification and apply while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: NHEC's current residential rebates use objective equipment and documentation requirements. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be paid after review, with additional verification for performance-based or whole-home incentive components.
reviews.evidenceText: Current NHEC pages list residential efficiency rebates and applications requiring member eligibility, qualifying equipment, invoices and installation details, and verification for specified higher-tier incentives.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible NHEC residential member at the proposed charger location.
Submit the current EV charging application and receive written preapproval before purchasing or installing the incentivized charging project.
Install eligible Level 2 charging equipment and the required meter-socket or time-of-use metering configuration using qualified electrical work.
Limit the claim to the current number of eligible chargers and comply with equipment, wiring, rate, and installation specifications.
Submit final invoices and installation records, pass inspection, and complete the project by the current program deadline while funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: NHEC's 2026 residential charging program has objective preapproval, equipment, metering, documentation, and inspection requirements. A written-approved project completed as specified is likely to receive the stated rebate, subject to first-come funding.
reviews.evidenceText: NHEC's current residential EV charging instructions require approval before installation, qualifying Level 2 equipment and metering, invoices, final inspection, and completion by the program deadline.

approvalRequirements: Construct an eligible new home in an Energy Trust participating utility territory.
Enroll the project early and work with an approved EPS verifier or other required program trade ally.
Design and build the home to the selected whole-home EPS pathway and exceed applicable code or program baselines, including insulation and envelope requirements.
Complete required plan review, site inspections, testing, modeling, and final energy-performance documentation.
Submit the final incentive package and comply with current completion deadlines, incentive caps, and available funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: EPS incentives are performance-based but follow a defined verifier and final-rating process rather than competitive selection. A home enrolled early and certified under an eligible pathway is likely to receive the applicable incentive, although insulation alone is not a standalone award basis.
reviews.evidenceText: Energy Trust's current EPS New Homes program requires early coordination with a verifier, above-code whole-home performance, inspections and testing, and a final qualifying rating before incentives are paid.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Jersey Natural Gas residential customer with an existing qualifying home.
Install currently qualifying HVAC or water-heating equipment, or enter the current whole-home efficiency pathway for eligible envelope and comprehensive measures.
For whole-home work, complete the required assessment and use an approved participating contractor or program process before implementing the project.
Submit the current application within the published filing period with a paid itemized receipt, permit documentation, model and efficiency information, and other required records.
Allow verification and comply with equipment-installation dates, incentive caps, and available program funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SAVEGREEN's current prescriptive and whole-home offerings use published eligibility and documentation requirements. A conforming claim is likely after review, although the current official pages do not substantiate every legacy mapped measure, including a general laundry rebate.
reviews.evidenceText: Current SAVEGREEN materials provide residential HVAC, water-heating, and whole-home efficiency pathways with equipment or assessment requirements, filing deadlines, paid receipts, permits, and verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible existing New Jersey Natural Gas commercial customer and select a current SAVEGREEN business pathway.
Submit the project application, scope, equipment information, cost data, and savings or engineering documentation required for prescriptive, custom, Direct Install, or engineered work.
Obtain project and financing approval before construction when the selected pathway or on-bill repayment option requires it.
Satisfy any credit, repayment, customer-account, cost-effectiveness, contractor, and agreement conditions for on-bill financing.
Complete the approved project and submit invoices, permits, commissioning or savings records, and other closeout documentation for verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: SAVEGREEN business projects have established technical and financing pathways, but on-bill financing depends on project approval and customer-specific repayment or underwriting conditions. The current sources support efficiency projects, not the mapped standalone battery-storage system.
reviews.evidenceText: Current SAVEGREEN business materials require pathway-specific project review, supporting technical and cost documents, financing approval where requested, completed installation, and final verification. Standalone battery storage was not verified as an eligible measure.

approvalRequirements: No new SmartStart Buildings application can be approved because the program closed to new applications on October 31, 2025.
A project already accepted under the legacy program must continue under its existing approval, completion, and closeout requirements.
A new construction project must instead apply to the current New Construction Program and receive the required project approval before proceeding.
A retrofit project must use the applicable current utility-administered efficiency program rather than the closed SmartStart pathway.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The named SmartStart Buildings program is closed to new applications. Only previously accepted legacy projects may have a remaining payment path; new projects must use successor or utility programs.
reviews.evidenceText: New Jersey's current official site identifies SmartStart Buildings as a past program closed to new applications and directs new construction projects to the successor New Construction Program.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Mexico Gas Company nonresidential customer at the project location.
Install a currently qualifying high-efficiency natural-gas measure or propose an eligible custom project with documented energy savings.
Submit the applicable application, equipment specifications, cost information, and required business or account documentation.
Obtain program approval before purchase or installation for custom, assessment-driven, or other projects that require advance review.
Submit final invoices, installation and savings records, and allow inspection or other verification before payment while funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current commercial portfolio includes prescriptive rebates, assessments, and custom incentives under defined eligibility and review processes. A qualifying prescriptive claim or approved custom project is likely to be paid after documentation and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: NMGC's current business program offers qualifying equipment rebates, assessments, and custom incentives, with applications, technical and cost documentation, advance review for project-specific work, and final verification.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Mexico Gas Company residential customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying natural-gas heating measure, smart thermostat, insulation measure, or other listed residential improvement.
Meet the current equipment-efficiency, contractor, installation, testing, and existing-condition requirements for the selected measure.
Submit the current rebate application with an itemized invoice, model and efficiency information, contractor documentation, and any required photographs or test results.
Allow program review or verification and apply within the current filing period while funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: NMGC's current residential rebates use objective customer, equipment, and documentation criteria. A complete qualifying application is likely to be paid after validation, subject to current incentive limits and funding.
reviews.evidenceText: Current NMGC residential pages provide heating, thermostat, and insulation rebates and require qualifying equipment or work, invoices, model and contractor records, and program review.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Prague Utilities commercial or industrial electric customer.
Select a measure covered by the current 2026 business forms or submit a qualifying custom project through the utility contact process.
Meet the current equipment-efficiency, operating, savings, installation, and customer requirements for the selected measure.
Obtain advance utility approval for custom or other projects whose application requires preapproval before ordering or installation.
Submit the signed measure-specific application with itemized invoices, specifications, calculations where required, and verification records while funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: New Prague and SMMPA publish current business forms covering many mapped efficiency measures and a custom-project route. A qualifying prescriptive claim or preapproved custom project is likely to receive the calculated rebate after review and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Current New Prague and SMMPA materials link 2026 commercial forms for lighting, HVAC, refrigeration, motors, controls, compressed air, and custom projects, with applications, technical documentation, and utility review.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Prague Utilities residential electric customer.
Purchase and install a measure covered by the current 2026 residential rebate forms, such as qualifying heating, cooling, water-heating, appliance, or EV charging equipment.
Meet the applicable equipment rating, installation, customer, quantity, and existing-system requirements.
Submit the signed current application with itemized invoices, model numbers, efficiency certificates, and other required purchase or installation records.
Apply within the current program period and allow utility verification while rebate funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current residential rebates are prescriptive and use published forms and equipment criteria. A complete, timely qualifying claim is likely to be paid after routine utility review, subject to funds and measure caps.
reviews.evidenceText: New Prague's current rebate page links 2026 residential forms for qualifying equipment and EV charging and requires customer eligibility, invoices, technical details, and utility review.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Mexico taxpayer who owns the qualifying solar system at a residence, business, or agricultural enterprise in New Mexico.
Install and place in operation qualifying photovoltaic or solar-thermal equipment; a standalone battery system is not eligible for this credit.
Complete required permitting, code inspection, utility or jurisdictional approval, and retain ownership, invoice, site-plan, and technical documentation.
Apply online to the Energy, Minerals and Natural Resources Department within one calendar year after the system is installed for an eligibility certificate.
After certification, claim the approved credit through the Taxation and Revenue Department, subject to the per-system and annual program caps.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The credit is statutory and uses objective system, ownership, documentation, and certification rules rather than competitive scoring. A qualifying certified system is likely to receive the credit, subject to the annual aggregate cap and tax administration.
reviews.evidenceText: New Mexico's current guide provides a credit of up to ten percent of eligible solar-system cost, capped per system, and requires an operating owned system, permits and inspection, an EMNRD certificate, and a later tax claim. Standalone batteries are excluded.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible New Ulm Public Utilities residential or commercial customer for the selected current rebate.
Purchase and install equipment listed in the current 2026 rebate materials and meet the applicable efficiency, sizing, installation, and customer requirements.
Use the correct current residential or commercial application and comply with measure-specific qualifications.
Submit a detailed itemized invoice, model and efficiency information, required certifications, and a signed application by the published filing deadline.
Allow utility review or inspection and apply while current-year program funds remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: New Ulm publishes current-year forms and objective measure criteria, making payment likely for a complete qualifying claim. The source mapping is broader than the verified 2026 catalog, which does not clearly support every listed retrofit such as standalone battery storage or all water measures.
reviews.evidenceText: New Ulm's 2026 materials require current qualifying equipment, a signed measure-specific form, detailed invoices, model and efficiency documentation, timely filing, and utility review. Several mapped measures are not shown in the verified current catalog.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible New York City Class 1, Class 2, or Class 4 property with qualifying photovoltaic or energy-storage equipment.
Place the qualifying equipment in service during the statutory eligibility period ending December 31, 2034.
Use a New York State licensed professional engineer or registered architect and obtain all required Department of Buildings and electrical permits, inspections, and approvals.
Document eligible expenditures, exclude grants or other disallowed amounts, and professionally certify the property-tax-abatement application.
Submit the application through the Department of Buildings HUB by the statutory deadline and satisfy ongoing compliance and Department of Finance processing requirements.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The abatement is statutory and calculated from eligible expenditures rather than awarded competitively. A compliant PV or storage installation with professional certification and complete DOB filing is likely to receive the abatement, subject to statutory caps and tax processing; biomass is not supported by the current eligibility evidence.
reviews.evidenceText: Current New York law extends the NYC property-tax abatement to qualifying photovoltaic and energy-storage equipment placed in service through 2034. DOB requires licensed-professional filing, permits, eligible-cost disclosure, certification, and HUB submission.
